moat: Automotive OEM coatings
Wide
No.1 with ~61% share (FY24) and 61-81% at the largest 2/3-wheeler makers; Kansai Paint's global auto technology; 200-300 technical staff on customer lines; long approval cycles.
The best business in the company; switching costs are real but OEMs push back on price.
Powder coatings
Narrow
No.1 'for more than two decades' (MD); broad customer approvals in appliances, furniture, auto parts.
Leadership in a fragmented, price-competitive market.
Performance and general industrial liquids
Narrow
No.3; growing double digit in infrastructure, railways, coil coating, PEB.
Growth, but against Asian PPG, Berger, Akzo/JSW, Jotun.
Decorative brand
Eroding
No.2 top-of-mind brand recall (company); jingle known for 30+ years; but revenue growth ~0-5% for three years while Birla Opus reached ~10% share in two.
Awareness does not equal pricing power: Nerolac follows, it does not lead.
Decorative distribution
None
35,000+ dealers vs new entrants who reached every corner within two years; 'network addition of 5-10% a year'.
Rivals bought shelf space quickly; distribution was not a barrier.
Cost position
None
Gross margin ~35% in Q1FY27 vs ~41-45% for Asian Paints, Berger and Indigo (Screener, Q1FY27 material cost 55-59%); no raw-material backward integration ('not yet on the card').
Mix explains part of it; there is no cost advantage.
Parent's technology
Narrow
Access to Kansai Paint R&D and group sourcing for a royalty of ~0.4% of standalone sales (Rs32.7 cr, FY26).
Cheap and valuable in industrial; little help in Indian decorative retail.
critiques: Decorative is losing ground: Birla Opus alone booked Rs1,661 cr in Q1FY27, more than Nerolac's whole decorative business on management's own split; Nerolac's claim to be No.3 looks lost.
FY27 growth is mostly price: ~5% in Q1 and ~8% for the year after the Q2 rises, with decorative volumes growing only low single digit.
The 13-14% margin guidance has been repeated for years: met only at the bottom in FY25 (13.0% standalone) and missed in FY26 (12.7% standalone, 12.1% consolidated).
Two land sales (Rs1,327 cr of gains) made FY24-25 earnings look twice their real level; underlying EPS has been flat at ~Rs8 for three years.
Overseas subsidiaries destroyed value: ~Rs211 cr of impairments in FY24-26 (standalone) and Sri Lanka sold for ~Rs5 lakh; Bangladesh still loses money.
Rs2,500 cr of cash earns ~6% while ROE is ~9-10%; payout is only ~33% outside the land-sale specials.

Bull case: industrial (~55% of sales) is a high-quality, growing franchise valued at a fraction of peers; at ~18x FY28E the stock prices the whole company as if it were a declining decorative business.
GAM, drawing on PL, ICICI Securities and Nomura (2025)
